description: §5.2.1/§5.2.2 a `${…}` expression-form handler holding two `;`-separated statements runs BOTH when the first one is a call. #x: `@items.push(1); @last = 2`; #y: `f(); g()` (f adds 1, g multiplies by 10). Was carried on impl#1 (S432, P7: every statement after a leading call was dropped); resolved S437.
rationale: §5.2.1: "`onclick=${expr}` on an event attribute SHALL use the `${...}` expression directly as the event handler, with `@var` references rewritten to reactive getters." E-MULTI-STATEMENT-HANDLER (§5.2.3) is scoped to the BARE form; the `${}` form carries its logic content verbatim, and impl#1 already runs both statements when the first is an assignment (`${@a = 1; @b = 2}`). Nothing makes the second statement's fate depend on whether the first is a call. After #x then #y: items is [1]; last is 2 after #x, then f → 3, g → 30.
